canonicalCards.recommendedFirstExperiment: Use Stereo Pan or Direction Mixer to reduce width gradually, then compare the source in mono, stereo, and full arrangement.
stopOrUndo: Stop once a focused position with enough internal stereo character to retain identity is repeatably improved in context. Back off or undo if collapsing to mono can cancel side information or change tone when the recording contains phase differences..
Bypass the changed processor or restore the saved pan, polarity, delay, width, routing, and automation values; remove any duplicate or diagnostic path created for the test.

canonicalCards.recommendedFirstExperiment: Verify Mid and Side channel assignment, decode at neutral width, and confirm that reducing Side to zero leaves only the Mid signal.
stopOrUndo: Stop once a stable center, controllable width, and predictable mono fold-down is repeatably improved in context. Back off or undo if wrong routing can create swapped image, cancellation, or excessive side level..
Bypass the changed processor or restore the saved pan, polarity, delay, width, routing, and automation values; remove any duplicate or diagnostic path created for the test.
canonicalCards.teachingPrinciple: M/S decoding requires the Mid channel and a duplicated polarity-opposed Side contribution; incorrect channel order or polarity breaks width and mono behavior.
canonicalCards.title: Decoding An M/S Microphone Recording — what it changes
tradeoffs: Wrong routing can create swapped image, cancellation, or excessive side level.
A change that increases apparent width or loudness may be preferred before mono translation and center stability are judged.
A local improvement can create a new balance, localization, depth, or arrangement problem.
canonicalCards.userIntent: Understand the underlying production concept and avoid a misleading shortcut.

contradictions.summary: Try polarity inversion first / Move or delay the signal first
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: A polarity flip is a fast binary diagnosis; time alignment is needed when arrival-time differences dominate. Compare both without changing level.

contradictions.summary: Sample-align every microphone / Preserve natural arrival differences
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Alignment can increase punch but may erase depth and room geometry. The role of each microphone and mono result decide.

contradictions.summary: Align by waveform peaks / Align by listening
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Visual landmarks help locate a range, but complex signals and different microphone responses require listening across several hits or notes.

contradictions.summary: Always invert the bottom snare mic / Test both polarities
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Opposite physical orientation often suggests inversion, but actual wiring, timing, bleed, and desired tone decide.

contradictions.summary: Use overheads as timing reference / Use close mics as timing reference
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: The reference should reflect the intended drum image: overhead-led natural kit versus close-mic impact.

contradictions.summary: Align room mics for punch / Keep room delay for size
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Partial alignment can be a compromise; compare punch, depth, groove, and mono rather than assuming one goal.

contradictions.summary: Align DI and amp exactly / Blend by ear without exact alignment
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Distortion and speaker response make exact waveform matching ambiguous; the intended low-end and attack decide.

contradictions.summary: Manually delay parallel paths / Trust plug-in delay compensation
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Manual delay is justified only after proving compensation is incomplete; otherwise it can double-correct.

contradictions.summary: Use linear phase to avoid phase shift / Use minimum phase for natural transient behavior
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Parallel interaction, latency, pre-ringing, source type, and audible result decide.

contradictions.summary: Keep correlation always above zero / Allow brief negative correlation for creative effects
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Critical mono stability and duration of negative excursions matter more than a universal meter target.

contradictions.summary: Stereo and mono should sound identical / Mono may change while remaining compatible
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Critical hierarchy and tone should survive; decorative width and ambience may change.

contradictions.summary: Match the reference track’s global width / Build width from the current arrangement
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Reference arrangement, loudness, and genre differ; role-based comparison is more useful than copying a width amount.

contradictions.summary: Boost Side for width / Reduce Mid for width
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Both alter Mid/Side balance differently in level and focus; matched-loudness stereo/mono comparison decides.

contradictions.summary: Use short delay for natural width / Avoid Haas widening because of mono combing
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Its value depends on source importance, delay time, dry center, and acceptable mono coloration.

contradictions.summary: Use duplicated delayed tracks / Record true doubles
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: True doubles usually provide more independent width; fake doubles may be valid when performance or style demands consistency.

contradictions.summary: Use chorus for width / Use micro-pitch for width
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Chorus adds movement; micro-pitch can be steadier. Pitch stability, modulation, and mono behavior decide.

contradictions.summary: Widen the mix bus / Widen selected sources only
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Global widening is efficient but affects every role; source-level arrangement usually offers more control.

contradictions.summary: Mono everything below a fixed frequency / Preserve contextual low-frequency stereo
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Format, source, room, and translation decide; no universal crossover applies.

contradictions.summary: Remove all low Side information / Keep natural stereo bass information
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Stability must be balanced against acoustic scale and room realism.

contradictions.summary: Collapse stereo piano to mono / Keep a wide piano perspective
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: The piano’s role, arrangement density, mono cancellation, and low-end stability decide.

contradictions.summary: Use Balance for stereo tracks / Use Stereo Pan or Direction Mixer
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Balance is fine at center or when attenuating a side is intended; Stereo Pan preserves both channels during repositioning.

contradictions.summary: Hard-pan doubles / Use moderate pan positions
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Hard panning maximizes separation; moderate positions may feel more cohesive, especially on headphones.

contradictions.summary: Always center lead vocal / Pan lead vocal creatively
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Centering supports focus and mono; off-center placement can be valid when arrangement and effects provide a deliberate counterweight.

contradictions.summary: Always center bass / Pan bass for artistic effect
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Keep critical low energy stable, but higher harmonics or deliberate arrangements can support off-center bass.

contradictions.summary: Make left and right symmetrical / Use intentional asymmetry
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Energy balance and musical counterweight matter more than mirror symmetry.

contradictions.summary: Pan competing parts apart / Fix masking with arrangement/EQ/level
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Panning helps stereo separation but conflicts may return in mono; multiple dimensions may be needed.

contradictions.summary: Build the whole mix in mono first / Mix in stereo with frequent mono checks
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Mono-first exposes conflicts; stereo-first preserves spatial intent. Workflow preference and results decide.

contradictions.summary: Use audience perspective / Use drummer perspective
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Consistency and artistic intent matter more than a universal perspective.

contradictions.summary: Pan the send / Pan the return
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Send pan changes how one source enters a processor; return pan moves the combined effect. Shared routing decides.

contradictions.summary: Pan ambience opposite the dry source / Keep ambience with the dry source
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Opposite placement creates counterbalance; same-side placement reinforces localization. Clarity and cohesion decide.

contradictions.summary: Keep returns hard stereo / Narrow and position effect returns
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Wide returns create scale but can dominate sides and reduce source localization.

contradictions.summary: Use 0 dB pan law / Use -3 dB or compensated pan law
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Consistency within the project and cross-DAW translation matter more than one universally superior law.

contradictions.summary: Change pan law to fix center level / Leave pan law and rebalance tracks
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Changing global law can invalidate existing balances; rebalance is usually safer after a mix is underway.

contradictions.summary: Use binaural panning for more realism / Use conventional stereo panning for compatibility
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Headphone-first spatialization and speaker-first translation have different priorities.

contradictions.summary: Trust the correlation meter / Trust mono listening
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: The meter locates risk; listening establishes whether critical content actually fails.

contradictions.summary: Use an automatic phase-alignment plug-in / Adjust manually or at recording
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Automation can track changing relationships, but may introduce artifacts or obscure intentional depth.

contradictions.summary: Aim for a specific vectorscope shape / Use the scope only diagnostically
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Different arrangements create different valid shapes; audible balance and mono translation decide.

contradictions.summary: Widen a narrow X/Y recording artificially / Accept or re-record the original perspective
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Processing can add width but may undermine the technique’s coherence; musical need and mono behavior decide.

contradictions.summary: Time-align spaced microphones / Preserve spacing cues
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Alignment can improve mono but collapse intended spatial information.

contradictions.summary: Use M/S on every master / Use M/S only for a demonstrated issue
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: M/S is powerful but affects many sources and can create center/side imbalance.

contradictions.summary: Automate width for every chorus / Use arrangement contrast instead
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Width automation is one option; new layers, subtraction, and ambience may create stronger contrast.

contradictions.summary: Avoid hard pans for headphones / Use hard pans when arrangement supports them
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use a short reversible comparison before choosing.
contradictions.whatDecides: Headphone comfort, genre, counterweight, and speaker translation decide.

myths.correction: Polarity is a broadband sign inversion; phase shift is generally frequency- and time-dependent.
myths.myth: Polarity inversion and a 180-degree phase shift are always the same thing.

myths.correction: It only provides one binary inversion and may improve some frequencies while worsening others.
myths.myth: A polarity button fixes every phase problem.

myths.correction: Different spectra and microphone responses can still combine unpredictably.
myths.myth: If two waveforms line up visually, they are phase-correct.

myths.correction: Natural time differences can provide depth, room, and localization.
myths.myth: Every multi-mic track should be sample-aligned.

myths.correction: Maximum bass may sacrifice attack, bleed balance, or arrangement fit.
myths.myth: The fullest polarity setting is always correct.

myths.correction: Phase is relational unless a specific reference or playback path is named.
myths.myth: A single signal can be universally “out of phase” by itself.

myths.correction: Brief negative excursions can be intentional; sustained loss of critical content in mono is the real concern.
myths.myth: Negative correlation always means the mix is broken.

myths.correction: Frequency-specific cancellation or balance changes can remain hidden in a full-band value.
myths.myth: Correlation above zero guarantees good mono translation.

myths.correction: It mainly indicates similarity/mono-ness, not quality.
myths.myth: A vertical vectorscope is always better than a wide one.

myths.correction: Width can come from unstable or canceling side information.
myths.myth: A wide vectorscope proves a professional stereo image.

myths.correction: Compatible mono may legitimately lose decorative side detail while preserving critical roles.
myths.myth: Stereo and mono should sound identical.

myths.correction: Perceived width depends on contrast; widening everything can reduce focus and apparent width.
myths.myth: Wider is always better.

myths.correction: Identical or near-identical copies mainly add level and can comb-filter when delayed.
myths.myth: Duplicating and panning a track creates true stereo.

myths.correction: Any delayed duplicate can comb-filter in mono; severity depends on delay, spectrum, and level.
myths.myth: Haas delay is mono compatible if the delay is short enough.

myths.correction: Mid and Side are sum/difference components that can contain many sources.
myths.myth: Mid equals the lead vocal and Side equals the instruments.

myths.correction: Changing Side-to-Mid balance changes perceived hierarchy even if Mid gain is untouched.
myths.myth: Boosting Side only makes a mix wider, not quieter in the center.

myths.correction: The appropriate treatment depends on source, medium, room, and translation.
myths.myth: All low frequencies must be mono below one fixed number.

myths.correction: Upper harmonics and spatial ambience can be stereo while critical sub energy remains stable.
myths.myth: Stereo bass is always unsafe.

myths.correction: Balance attenuates one existing channel and can change the source.
myths.myth: A stereo file should always use the default Balance control.

myths.correction: They perform different operations on stereo signals.
myths.myth: Stereo Pan and Balance are two names for the same thing.

myths.correction: Pan law controls gain distribution during panning.
myths.myth: Pan law creates stereo width.

myths.correction: It can alter established balances and compensated extremes.
myths.myth: Changing pan law is a harmless preference at any time.

myths.correction: It is a valid spatial grammar when arrangement and headphone balance support it.
myths.myth: Hard panning is inherently amateur.

myths.correction: They can create a continuous stage or an indistinct cluster.
myths.myth: Intermediate pan positions are always more natural.

myths.correction: Intentional asymmetry can be stable when energy and narrative are counterweighted.
myths.myth: A mix must be perfectly symmetrical left to right.

myths.correction: The conflict can return in mono and reverberant playback.
myths.myth: Panning alone solves frequency masking.

myths.correction: Centering is common, but deliberate off-center or moving vocals can work with appropriate support.
myths.myth: Lead vocals must never move from center.

myths.correction: Center anchors are contextual, not mandatory.
myths.myth: Kick, bass, snare, and vocal must all be centered in every genre.

myths.correction: It is headphone-oriented spatial rendering with listener-dependent cues and different speaker translation.
myths.myth: Binaural panning is simply better stereo panning.

myths.correction: HRTF differences create listener-dependent localization and coloration.
myths.myth: Binaural placement will externalize identically for everyone.

myths.correction: Advanced controls are useful only when ordinary Stereo Pan cannot meet the need.
myths.myth: Direction Mixer is always better than the channel pan control.

myths.correction: It redistributes frequency information and can alter mono tone and correlation.
myths.myth: Stereo Spread is transparent because it only changes width.

myths.correction: It separates common and difference components, not object stems.
myths.myth: M/S processing isolates specific named instruments.

myths.correction: It can change the perceived center/side hierarchy and mono balance.
myths.myth: Side-only EQ cannot affect the center image.

myths.correction: It preserves relative phase through the filter but adds latency and may pre-ring.
myths.myth: Linear-phase EQ has no phase-related downside.

myths.correction: One time offset creates different phase angles by frequency.
myths.myth: Sample Delay can perfectly align every frequency of two complex recordings.

myths.correction: It may track noise/bleed, erase depth, or chase changing waveforms.
myths.myth: Automatic phase alignment always improves multi-mic recordings.

myths.correction: Phones, clubs, smart speakers, broadcast, accessibility, and partial listening positions still create mono or near-mono conditions.
myths.myth: Mono summing is only relevant to old radios.

myths.correction: The problem may be channel balance, recording perspective, or arrangement.
myths.myth: If a stereo source sounds louder on one side, it needs more widening.

myths.correction: It progressively attenuates the opposite channel.
myths.myth: Panning a stereo source with Balance moves the full image intact.

myths.correction: They act at different routing points and affect shared senders differently.
myths.myth: Send pan and return pan produce the same spatial result.

myths.correction: Same-side and opposite-side ambience produce different localization and counterbalance.
myths.myth: Reverb should always be panned with the dry source.

myths.correction: Arrangement, new layers, ambience, and source panning may create cleaner contrast.
myths.myth: Every chorus should become wider through a master widener.

myths.correction: Visual balance does not account for spectral energy, perception, or room asymmetry.
myths.myth: If the meter looks balanced, the mix is balanced.

myths.correction: It changes orientation but not timing or polarity relationships within channels.
myths.myth: Swapping left and right fixes phase problems.

myths.correction: A reversible Gain plug-in test preserves source and alternatives.
myths.myth: Destructively inverting a file is the best first polarity test.

myths.correction: Panning changes level distribution; cancellation depends on channel relationships and playback.
myths.myth: Panning a low-frequency source off-center always causes phase cancellation.

myths.correction: Different performances usually sum as a thicker mono texture, though timing/pitch interactions can still change tone.
myths.myth: Two hard-panned true doubles will always cancel in mono.

myths.correction: Noncritical ambience can change if the core musical message remains stable.
myths.myth: Decorrelated stereo ambience must be eliminated because it changes in mono.

myths.correction: Valid correlation varies with arrangement, ambience, frequency, and time.
myths.myth: There is one ideal correlation value for a finished mix.
